tests.name: test_dense_dy_band_uses_quadratic_mean_and_delta_variance
tests.claim: For a dense bilinear operator, _bilinear_predictive_band's mean is E[q^T Y q] and its std is a delta-method propagation of the GP covariance through 2*sym(Y)*mean.
tests.actual: Recomputes both quantities independently in the test body (no call to any source helper for the 'expected' side) from the stated closed forms, then compares to the real, unmocked runner._bilinear_predictive_band output. Parametrized over the 4 runner aliases, which are 2 distinct plot_datasets.py bodies run twice each (module docstring).
tests.how: np.einsum contraction of the same operator/mean/covariance the source uses, built independently in the test; runner._bilinear_predictive_band internally calls the real pixel.core.evidence._bilinear_prediction_from_second for the mean and a local _bilinear_symmetric_action for the gradient half.
tests.bar: np.testing.assert_allclose bare default (rtol=1e-7, atol=0); a standalone pixel.core.evidence reproduction of this exact input measured 0.0 relative difference
tests.catches: a wrong einsum contraction index, a missing symmetrization of Y, or a missing factor of 2 (unsymmetrized gradient) or 4 in the delta-method variance. Does NOT establish that the delta-method variance is a good approximation to the true (non-Gaussian) DY posterior variance -- that is a documented modeling choice in the source, not something this test addresses.

tests.name: test_factorized_dy_band_matches_equivalent_dense_operator
tests.claim: The factorized BilinearFactorBlock code path produces the same DY band as an algebraically equivalent dense tensor.
tests.actual: Builds one BilinearFactorBlock and a hand-derived dense tensor via einsum('ab,rij->raibj',...).reshape(...), with scale baked into the dense tensor and applied post-hoc for the factorized case; calls the SAME runner._bilinear_predictive_band wrapper on both and compares mean and std at rtol=1e-12. Exercises only a single factorized block.
tests.how: Two calls to the identical wrapper function, differing only in the type of blocks.bilinear_Y passed (tuple-of-BilinearFactorBlock vs. dense ndarray).
tests.catches: a wrong mixing/tensor contraction index or transposition in the factorized branch specifically -- demonstrated by mutant: transposing the mixing indices (einsum('ba,rij->...') for einsum('ab,rij->...')) breaks agreement by 3.4e-2, ten orders above the bar. Does NOT catch a bug in code the two branches share (second-moment construction, clip, sqrt -- test 1 covers that with an independent oracle instead), and does not exercise more than one factorized block at once, so the action[sl] += / prediction.at[...].add accumulation across multiple blocks is untested here.

tests.name: test_mixed_records_include_linear_and_dy_without_rebuilding_short_samples
tests.claim: build_records_from_result produces both a linear and a dy record, using the full merged representative vector (not a short per-sample row) even when the sampler's stored .samples array is smaller than the model's free-parameter count.
tests.actual: The rebuild stub's embedded 'assert vec.size == 3' is the real, discriminating check: it fires if _representative_vector (via the monkeypatched fitmod._weighted_mean_vec) ever falls back to something other than the model-aware 3-vector. The kind-SET equality check only proves one record of each kind is present (blind to duplicates or extra records); the 'linear' record's own fields are never separately inspected; the DY record's x/xlabel are checked against an exact numeric coincidence (Q2/S=0.25); fit_std/chi2_per_data are checked for sign/finiteness only, not value.
tests.how: Hand-built Model/samples/blocks SimpleNamespaces; fitmod._weighted_mean_vec is monkeypatched to mimic the real function's documented two-arity NestedVegasSamples contract (short vector without model=, full vector with it, per closure_JAM_truth_small/fit.py:474-484); model._rebuild/_blocks are local closures, with the assertion inside _rebuild standing in for a numeric oracle.
tests.bar: exact size==3 in the rebuild mock (load-bearing); assert_allclose bare default for x; strict >0.0 and isfinite for fit_std/chi2_per_data
tests.catches: a regression where build_records_from_result (or _representative_vector) passes a short/unmerged sample vector into model._rebuild instead of the full n_free representative vector -- a real, documented failure mode of fit._weighted_mean_vec's NestedVegasSamples branch. Does NOT catch a wrong numeric DY band value, a duplicated record, or a wrong 'linear' record field.

tests.name: test_dy_records_render_png_and_pdf
tests.claim: plot_records writes both a PNG and a PDF for a DY-kind record.
tests.actual: Checks only Path.is_file() for the given .png path and its .with_suffix('.pdf') sibling, after a real, unmocked call. No assertion inspects the Figure/Axes: no check of line data, fill_between extents, axis scale, legend, title, or the DY footnote text.
tests.how: One hand-built record dict (x.size==3, use_log=False) fed to the real plot_records; output written under tmp_path.
tests.catches: a dropped output format, a wrong suffix-derivation in save_figure_both, or an exception from a malformed/mismatched record (wrong array lengths, missing keys). Does NOT catch wrong rendered content (wrong data, wrong color, wrong scale, missing legend/title/footnote) -- pixel.plotting's sibling suite already has that pattern (tests/test_plotting.py:381, figures[1].axes[0].get_xscale()) and this file has no equivalent.

The byte-identity the RUNNERS docstring asserts in prose is now an assertion: both pairs are compared with read_bytes(), so any divergence -- including in main/write_summary/plot_records details no test reaches -- fails loudly instead of quietly voiding the 4-way parametrization's stated purpose. RUNNERS is kept at 4 entries (drift insurance). Acceptance: the same comparison applied to a genuinely different pair (full vs _small, which differ inside _truth_predictions) returns False, so the assertion is not vacuous; measured sha256 cf44fa450537e9af... for the full pair and adbee46c46c646b0... for the _small pair. tests/test_closure_dy_plotting.py:70 RUNNERS = (jam_full, jam_small, nnpdf_full, nnpdf_small). Measured this audit: `diff closure_JAM_truth/plot_datasets.py closure_NNPDF_truth/plot_datasets.py` exits 0 (byte-identical), and likewise `diff closure_JAM_truth_small/plot_datasets.py closure_NNPDF_truth_small/plot_datasets.py`.
weaknesses.why_it_matters: The 4-way parametrization on tests 1-2 runs 2 distinct plot_datasets.py bodies twice each under different names, not 4 independent implementations; a reader could believe 4 independently-maintained closure families are being cross-checked when only 2 code bodies exist today.
weaknesses.proposed_fix: Documentation only here (module docstring/RUNNERS comment now state the byte-identity and why it is kept anyway, as drift insurance). If the redundancy is unwanted, collapse RUNNERS to 2 entries, or add a dedicated test asserting the JAM/NNPDF plot_datasets.py pair stays identical so the intent is explicit.

weaknesses.evidence: RESOLVED 2026-08-14 by test_flat_samples_are_rejected_instead_of_silently_scaling_the_band and test_predictive_band_refuses_a_vector_weight_count_mismatch. The 1-D leg is no longer left unpinned: it is out of contract and now RAISES. All four plot_datasets.py copies changed identically (byte-identity between the JAM/NNPDF pair and between the _small pair preserved): _sample_vectors_and_weights refuses vectors.ndim != 2 (not just == 1, so a 3-D .samples -- which the old reshape passed through untouched -- is caught too), and _sampled_linear_predictive_band names a vector/weight count mismatch instead of letting zip() truncate. Justification is the sampler contract, not a preference: infer/hmc.py:1101 and infer/nuts.py:1100 allocate np.empty((n_samples, n_params)), infer/vegas.py:1036 and infer/mcmc.py:383 stack per-draw rows, and all four write the zero-parameter case as np.zeros((n_samples, 0)) -- still 2-D, and now pinned by a control. Acceptance: a plugin restoring the old reshape AND removing the zip guard (self-checked to apply) makes exactly the 12 new parametrized cases fail while the file's other 77 pass. Measured pre-fix damage: mean scaled by exactly 1/n (0.33333333 at n=3), band wrong by 1.09-1.36x in the other direction. STILL OPEN, with a partial mitigation added 2026-08-13 (deliberately not marked resolved): the new test_closure_symmetric_action_matches_the_pixel_core_evidence_copy checks the half-gradient against a genuinely separate implementation (pixel.core.evidence), so the piece of shared code most likely to be wrong is now cross-checked. The wrapper pieces this weakness names -- second-moment construction, the clip, the sqrt -- remain common-mode between the factorized and dense calls, and are covered instead by test_dense_dy_band_uses_quadratic_mean_and_delta_variance's independent closed form, exactly as the original entry says. No change to the test this weakness is filed against. tests/test_closure_dy_plotting.py:176-181 -- both factorized_result and dense_result are produced by the same runner._bilinear_predictive_band call; only the isinstance(Y, tuple) branch inside _bilinear_prediction_from_second/_bilinear_symmetric_action differs between the two calls.
weaknesses.why_it_matters: A bug in code the two branches share (second-moment construction 'second = covariance + outer(mean, mean)', the clip/sqrt wrapper, or the post-hoc scale multiply) would affect both calls identically and this test would still pass. This is inherent to what the test is for -- validating the factorized fast path against the dense path -- not a defect: test 1 independently covers the shared wrapper math with an unrelated, hand-derived oracle, so the two tests are complementary rather than either being weak alone.
weaknesses.proposed_fix: None needed; now stated explicitly in both the module and per-test docstrings. If isolated further, a from-scratch (non-wrapper) computation of the dense case, as test 1 already does, would remove the last shared-code sliver.

weaknesses.evidence: RESOLVED 2026-08-13 by test_mixed_records_include_linear_and_dy_without_rebuilding_short_samples. Added `len(records) == 2` beside the kind-set check, and seven value assertions on the previously-uninspected 'linear' record: xlabel, use_log, x, data, sigma, reproduction ([0.7, 0.9] -- B selects GP coefficients 0 and 1, so this is the first two entries of samples.mean), fit_std (sqrt of the first two diagonal entries of samples.covariance), truth ([0.6, 0.8]), and chi2 == 0.25 + 4/9 at rel=1e-12, all hand-derivable from the fixture. Acceptance: the record count now fails on a duplicated record, and the linear-band assertions fail under mutations of the shared band code (mut_plot.py MUT=band_between / band_weights reach the sampled path; the closed-form values here pin the stored-moments path). tests/test_closure_dy_plotting.py:288 `assert {record['kind'] for record in records} == {'linear', 'dy'}`; no assertion anywhere in the test checks len(records) or any field of the record whose kind == 'linear'.
weaknesses.why_it_matters: A bug that produced 3 or 4 records (e.g. a dataset double-counted across model._layout.datasets and .bilinear_datasets) would still satisfy the set equality; and a bug specific to the 'linear' record's construction (wrong x, wrong reproduction, wrong chi2) would pass entirely unnoticed since only the 'dy' record is pulled out and inspected.
weaknesses.proposed_fix: Assert len(records) == 2 alongside the kind check, and add at least one field assertion on the 'linear' record (e.g. its xlabel or chi2_per_data) mirroring what is already done for 'dy'.

weaknesses.evidence: RESOLVED 2026-08-13 by the new test_plot_records_renders_the_band_the_log_scale_and_the_dy_footnote and its control test_linear_only_records_carry_no_dy_footnote. plot_records closes its Figure before returning, so the test intercepts matplotlib.pyplot.close to keep it alive (the pattern tests/test_plotting.py:381 uses for pixel.plotting) and then asserts panel count, the fill_between band as a PolyCollection, the log scale, the per-panel title, and the DY footnote. test_dy_records_render_png_and_pdf is kept unchanged and unmocked for the file-writing path. missing.title: Exercise _sampled_linear_predictive_band/_sample_vectors_and_weights, the non-bilinear predictive-band path
missing.rationale: RESOLVED 2026-08-13 by three new tests: test_sampled_linear_band_mixes_per_sample_posterior_moments (the accumulation), test_sampled_linear_band_reuses_stored_moments_without_rebuilding (the cache short-circuit and its size guard), and test_sample_vectors_and_weights_handles_map_and_weighted_samples (the MAP and 2-D sample branches). Oracle: the law of total variance, sum_s w_s (var_s + mean_s^2) - (sum_s w_s mean_s)^2, written out in the test (A1 for the mixture combination) over per-sample moments from pixel.core.evidence.posterior (A3, shared with the source deliberately -- the accumulation is what is under test). Fixture is non-degenerate by measurement: with two samples at weights 0.25/0.75 and a per-sample param_pred offset of 4.0, dropping the between-sample term changes the reported std by 38.7% and equal weighting by 9.9%; the test asserts std/within_sample - 1 > 0.1 with 0.631 achieved. Acceptance: mut_plot.py MUT=band_between and MUT=band_weights each fail it; MUT=cache_guard fails the cache test. Achieved agreement 0.0 exactly for mean and std against a 1e-12 bar. FINDING, not closed: for a 1-D samples.samples array, _sample_vectors_and_weights returns ONE vector while fit._weights returns n weights (it reads samples.samples.shape[0] independently), and the caller's zip() then silently truncates and scales the whole band by 1/n. Which reading is right is a source question, so that leg is exercised but deliberately not pinned. closure_JAM_truth/plot_datasets.py:58-97 is the code path taken whenever model.has_bilinear is False or the sampler did not store marginalized GP moments (raw MCMC/NUTS/PosteriorResult samples) -- it distinguishes a MAP-like samples.x from a .samples array and averages with fitmod._weights. This file's only 'mixed records' test sets has_bilinear=True with valid samples.mean/.covariance, which takes the OTHER branch inside _posterior_predictive_bands and never reaches this one; samples.samples is set on the test's SimpleNamespace but is never actually read on that code path.

missing.title: Assert build_records_from_result sorts records by descending chi2
missing.rationale: RESOLVED 2026-08-13 by the new test_records_are_sorted_by_descending_chi2_with_nan_last, parametrized over RUNNERS.
